spec_notes: R-4 decides that repeated filter values all apply so conflicts select nothing; this changes the previous first-value behaviour for status and priority and is not marked as the builders' choice. R-1 says names follow the requester text conventions but also, in an unmarked line, measures the limit in Unicode code points, which the requester limit does not (it counts UTF-16 units); the 64-character limit itself is never written in the spec. R-1 pins 409 for a no-op request on a resolved/closed ticket (200 would also be correct). The spec is silent on keeping the assignee through transitions, on show printing it, on POST/PATCH refusing an assignee field and on the changelog/version. R-6 says "all four assignment tests" while the suite has seven (TC-4 (a), TC-5, TC-6 added later). Raw column and dash are marked as defaults.
tests_notes: TC-1 covers assignment, trimming, no-op, transition and patch shape, audit entries and actors, unassignment and notification delivery in one test; TC-4 covers legacy load, restart, notify file, CLI table, raw, show and the weekly report in one test. TC-4 (a) is tied to internals: it swaps service.store.persistence for a stub. TC-1 and TC-4 rely on service.worker.tick and service.notifier.delivered. Tests that would fail on another correct build: TC-1 expects three deliveries for Dana/Alex/Dana (agent-keyed dedupe keeping one for Dana is acceptable) and expects trimming; TC-2 expects 409 for a no-op on resolved/closed; TC-5 pins conflicting repeats -> [] and status=open&status=invalid -> 400; TC-6 pins code-point counting; TC-4 pins a dash in the table, a fifth raw column with an empty field and slices the table by the header width of ASSIGNEE (a longer name or another label would break it).
maintainer: Assignment is the only mutation with its own snapshot-and-restore around a failed save, so the store now has two failure behaviours, and the notification key depends on the audit sequence number, coupling outbox de-duplication to audit numbering. The data-file loader reuses the HTTP validator ticketAssignee, so tightening the request rule (length, characters) would silently make existing data files refuse to load. The shared intersectValues/CONFLICTING_FILTER logic in query.js also drives the CLI, so changing repeated-filter semantics changes both.
